claim: ULP-4 is a SUMO-specific peptidase in C. elegans.
source: ulp-4, a gene encoding ortholog of SUMO-specific peptidase in C. elegans, is one of the hits from our primary screen.
evidence: The text explicitly states that ulp-4 encodes a SUMO-specific peptidase ortholog in C. elegans.

claim: RNAi of ulp-4 impairs the activation of UPRmt induced by mitochondrial inhibitor antimycin A.
source: RNAi of ulp-4 impaired the activation of UPRmt that is induced by mitochondrial inhibitor antimycin A, or RNAi of nuclear encoded mitochondrial gene spg-7 (mitochondrial metalloprotease) (Figure 1A–B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, demonstrating that ulp-4 RNAi reduces UPRmt activation.

claim: RNAi of ulp-4 impairs the activation of UPRmt induced by RNAi of spg-7.
source: RNAi of ulp-4 impaired the activation of UPRmt that is induced by mitochondrial inhibitor antimycin A, or RNAi of nuclear encoded mitochondrial gene spg-7 (mitochondrial metalloprotease) (Figure 1A–B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Deficiency of ulp-4 suppresses the induction of endogenous mitochondrial chaperone gene hsp-6 under cco-1 RNAi.
source: Consistently, deficiency of ulp-4 also suppressed the induction of endogenous mitochondrial chaperone genes hsp-6 and hsp-60 under cco-1 RNAi (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Deficiency of ulp-4 suppresses the induction of endogenous mitochondrial chaperone gene hsp-60 under cco-1 RNAi.
source: Consistently, deficiency of ulp-4 also suppressed the induction of endogenous mitochondrial chaperone genes hsp-6 and hsp-60 under cco-1 RNAi (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The transcript level of ulp-4 is elevated during mitochondrial stress.
source: Notably, transcript level of ulp-4 was also elevated during mitochondrial stress (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: ulp-4 RNAi does not affect the induction of ER stress reporter hsp-4p::gfp.
source: In contrast, ulp-4 RNAi did not affect the induction of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress reporter hsp-4p::gfp nor heat shock stress reporter hsp-16.2p::gfp (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D-E.

claim: ulp-4 RNAi does not affect the induction of heat shock stress reporter hsp-16.2p::gfp.
source: In contrast, ulp-4 RNAi did not affect the induction of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress reporter hsp-4p::gfp nor heat shock stress reporter hsp-16.2p::gfp (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D-E.

claim: Worms treated with ulp-4 RNAi are still able to induce the expression of endogenous hsp-4 during ER stress.
source: In addition, worms treated with ulp-4 RNAi were still able to induce the expression of endogenous hsp-4 or hsp-16.2 during ER or heat shock stress (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Worms treated with ulp-4 RNAi are still able to induce the expression of endogenous hsp-16.2 during heat shock stress.
source: In addition, worms treated with ulp-4 RNAi were still able to induce the expression of endogenous hsp-4 or hsp-16.2 during ER or heat shock stress (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: RNAi of ulp-4 from L1 stage only delays worm development slightly.
source: RNAi of ulp-4 from L1 stage only delayed worm development a bit (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Overexpression of ULP-4 in ulp-4 RNAi worms rescues UPRmt activation.
source: Overexpression of ULP-4 in ulp-4 RNAi worms rescued UPRmt activation (Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The induction of UPRmt is impaired in ulp-4(tm1597) mutants.
source: Lastly, we crossed an ulp-4(tm1597) mutant allele that lacks 404nt in the promoter region of ulp-4 with hsp-6p::gfp reporter, and showed that the induction of UPRmt was also impaired in ulp-4 mutants (Figure 1H–I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H-I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Deficiency of ulp-1, 2, or 5 does not suppress antimycin-induced UPRmt.
source: Deficiency of ulp-1, 2, or 5 failed to suppress antimycin- or spg-7 RNAi-induced UPRmt (Figure 1K), suggesting a specific role of ulp-4 in mediating UPRmt.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1K.

claim: Deficiency of ulp-1, 2, or 5 does not suppress spg-7 RNAi-induced UPRmt.
source: Deficiency of ulp-1, 2, or 5 failed to suppress antimycin- or spg-7 RNAi-induced UPRmt (Figure 1K), suggesting a specific role of ulp-4 in mediating UPRmt.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1K.

claim: ULP-4 has a specific role in mediating UPRmt.
source: Deficiency of ulp-1, 2, or 5 failed to suppress antimycin- or spg-7 RNAi-induced UPRmt (Figure 1K), suggesting a specific role of ulp-4 in mediating UPRmt.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that only ulp-4, but not other ULPs, affects UPRmt.

claim: The only conserved region among ulp-1, 2, 4 and 5 is the catalytic domain.
source: Sequence alignment (Katoh and Standley, 2013) of ulp-1, 2, 4 and 5 revealed that the only conserved region among them is the catalytic domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: RNAi of the E1 SUMO activating enzyme aos-1 induces UPRmt more potently.
source: Conversely, RNAi of the E1 SUMO activating enzyme aos-1 or the E2 SUMO conjugating enzyme ubc-9 in C. elegans induced UPRmt more potently (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A-C.

claim: RNAi of the E2 SUMO conjugating enzyme ubc-9 induces UPRmt more potently.
source: Conversely, RNAi of the E1 SUMO activating enzyme aos-1 or the E2 SUMO conjugating enzyme ubc-9 in C. elegans induced UPRmt more potently (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A-C.

claim: RNAi of smo-1 induces only weak UPRmt under unstressed condition.
source: Moreover, RNAi of smo-1, the only SUMO ortholog gene in C. elegans, induced only weak UPRmt under unstressed condition (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3D-E.

claim: Upon mitochondrial stress, smo-1 RNAi further activates UPRmt.
source: However, upon mitochondrial stress, smo-1 RNAi further activated UPRmt (Figure 1—figure supplement 3F–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3F-G.

claim: smo-1 RNAi rescues ulp-4 deficiency-suppressed UPRmt.
source: More importantly, smo-1 RNAi rescued ulp-4 deficiency-suppressed UPRmt (Figure 1—figure supplement 3F–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3F-G.

claim: ULP-4 plays a specific role to mediate mitochondrial stress response through its SUMO peptidase activity.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that ULP-4 plays a specific role to mediate mitochondrial stress response through its SUMO peptidase activity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective experimental results showing that ULP-4 specifically affects UPRmt and that its effect can be rescued by smo-1 RNAi.

claim: DVE-1 interacts with ULP-4.
source: We found that DVE-1, a homeodomain-containing transcription factor in UPRmt (Haynes et al., 2007), interacted with ULP-4 (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast two-hybrid data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: DVE-1 can specifically interact with ULP-4, but not ULP-2 or ULP-5.
source: Notably, DVE-1 could specifically interact with ULP-4, but not ULP-2 or ULP-5 (Note: overexpression of ULP-1 in yeast is lethal) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast two-hybrid data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: smo-1 is one of the top hits from yeast two-hybrid screen with DVE-1 as bait.
source: Consistently, smo-1 is one of the top hits from our yeast two-hybrid screen with DVE-1 as bait (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast two-hybrid screen data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Only wild type SMO-1 or SMO-1 GG', but not SMO-1 ΔGG, interacts with DVE-1.
source: Only wild type SMO-1 or SMO-1 GG', but not SMO-1 ΔGG, interacted with DVE-1 (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), indicating that SMO-1 either covalently modifies DVE-1, or covalently modifies an adaptor protein that associates with DVE-1.
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast two-hybrid data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: SMO-1 either covalently modifies DVE-1, or covalently modifies an adaptor protein that associates with DVE-1.
source: Only wild type SMO-1 or SMO-1 GG', but not SMO-1 ΔGG, interacted with DVE-1 (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), indicating that SMO-1 either covalently modifies DVE-1, or covalently modifies an adaptor protein that associates with DVE-1.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that only active forms of SMO-1 interact with DVE-1.

claim: SUMOylated DVE-1 can be detected in worms.
source: SUMOylated DVE-1 could be detected in worms, the level of which was elevated under ulp-4 RNAi (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The level of SUMOylated DVE-1 is elevated under ulp-4 RNAi.
source: SUMOylated DVE-1 could be detected in worms, the level of which was elevated under ulp-4 RNAi (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: DVE-1 301–468 associates with SMO-1.
source: We found that DVE-1 301–468 associated with SMO-1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E), suggesting that SUMOylation site may resides in 301–468 amino acids of DVE-1.
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast two-hybrid data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: K327R mutation of DVE-1 abolishes SMO-1-DVE-1 interaction.
source: K327R, but not other mutations, abolished SMO-1-DVE-1 interaction (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast two-hybrid data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: SUMOylation of DVE-1 can be detected when wild type DVE-1, but not DVE-1 K327R, is expressed with SMO-1 and E2 conjugating enzyme UBC9 in 293 T cells.
source: Furthermore, SUMOylation of DVE-1 could be detected when we expressed wild type, but not DVE-1 K327R, with SMO-1 and E2 conjugating enzyme UBC9 in 293 T cells (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: SUMOylation of DVE-1 on K327 residue is observed in C. elegans.
source: Consistently, SUMOylation of DVE-1 on K327 residue was also observed in C. elegans (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: SMO-1 covalently modifies K327 residue of DVE-1.
source: Taken together, these results suggested that SMO-1 covalently modifies K327 residue of DVE-1.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective experimental results showing that K327 is the SUMOylation site of DVE-1.

claim: Induction of ULP-4, but not ULP-5, prevents yeast growth caused by SMO-1-DVE-1 interaction.
source: Induction of ULP-4, but not ULP-5, prevented yeast growth caused by SMO-1-DVE-1 interaction (Figure 2G), suggesting that ULP-4 may removes SUMO moiety from DVE-1.
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast three-hybrid data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: ULP-4 may remove SUMO moiety from DVE-1.
source: Induction of ULP-4, but not ULP-5, prevented yeast growth caused by SMO-1-DVE-1 interaction (Figure 2G), suggesting that ULP-4 may removes SUMO moiety from DVE-1.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the yeast three-hybrid experiment showing that ULP-4 disrupts SMO-1-DVE-1 interaction.

claim: Overexpression of ULP-4 in worms decreases SUMOylation level of DVE-1.
source: Overexpression of ULP-4 in worms decreased SUMOylation level of DVE-1 (Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Expression of ULP-4 C48 in 293 T cells can deSUMOylate DVE-1 in mammalian cells.
source: In addition, expression of ULP-4 C48, the catalytic domain of ULP-4 (Letunic and Bork, 2018) in 293 T cells could deSUMOylate DVE-1 in mammalian cells (Figure 2I).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: A CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in strain with DVE-1 K327R mutation bypasses the requirement of ulp-4 and is capable to activate UPRmt under ulp-4 RNAi.
source: Indeed, we found that a CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in strain with DVE-1 K327R mutation bypassed the requirement of ulp-4 and was capable to activate UPRmt under ulp-4 RNAi (Figure 2J and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2J and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: During mitochondrial stress, DVE-1 translocates from cytosol to nucleus.
source: During mitochondrial stress, DVE-1 translocates from cytosol to nucleus (Haynes et al., 2007; Tian et al., 2016) (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-B and citations to previous studies.

claim: Inactivation of ulp-4 by RNAi abolishes the nuclear accumulation of DVE-1 in cco-1 RNAi-treated worms.
source: Inactivation of ulp-4 by RNAi abolished the nuclear accumulation of DVE-1 in cco-1 RNAi-treated worms (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: Overexpression of ulp-4 increases the nuclear accumulation of DVE-1.
source: Conversely, overexpression of ulp-4 increased the nuclear accumulation of DVE-1 (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The induction of UPRmt correlates well with DVE-1 subcellular localization.
source: More importantly, we found that the induction of UPRmt correlated well with DVE-1 subcellular localization.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental observations described in Figure 3E.

claim: DVE-1 K327R constitutively localizes in the nucleus of C. elegans, even if ulp-4 is knocked down by RNAi.
source: Different from wild type proteins, DVE-1 K327R constitutively localized in the nucleus of C. elegans, even if ulp-4 was knocked down by RNAi (Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: SUMO-mimetic DVE-1 constitutively localizes in the cytosol.
source: Conversely, SUMO-mimetic DVE-1 constitutively localized in the cytosol (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: During mitochondrial stress, ULP-4 deSUMOylates DVE-1 at K327 residue to allow its nuclear accumulation to initiate UPRmt.
source: Taken together, during mitochondrial stress, ULP-4 deSUMOylates DVE-1 at K327 residue to allow its nuclear accumulation to initiate UPRmt.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective experimental results showing that ULP-4 deSUMOylates DVE-1 and that this affects DVE-1 localization and UPRmt activation.

claim: A fragment of ATFS-1 (372–472) is able to interact with ULP-4.
source: Aside from DVE-1, we found that a fragment of ATFS-1 (372–472), another transcription factor in UPRmt, was also able to interact with ULP-4 (Figure 4A, note: expression of full-length ATFS-1 is toxic in yeast).
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast two-hybrid data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: ATFS-1 can only interact with ULP-4, but not ULP-2 and ULP-5.
source: Similar as DVE-1, ATFS-1 could only interact with ULP-4, but not ULP-2 and ULP-5 (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by yeast two-hybrid data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: K326 residue is the bona fide ATFS-1 SUMOylation site.
source: In vivo SUMOylation assay in 293 T cells identified K326 residue as the bona fide ATFS-1 SUMOylation site (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: SUMOylation of ATFS-1 is observed in C. elegans.
source: SUMOylation of ATFS-1 was also observed in C. elegans, which could be abolished by mutating K326 residue to arginine (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Mutating K326 residue to arginine abolishes SUMOylation of ATFS-1 in C. elegans.
source: SUMOylation of ATFS-1 was also observed in C. elegans, which could be abolished by mutating K326 residue to arginine (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Expression of ULP-4 C48 in 293 T cells deSUMOylates ATFS-1.
source: Expression of ULP-4 C48, the catalytic domain of ULP-4, in 293 T cells deSUMOylated ATFS-1 (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Expression of ATFS-1 K326R in atfs-1(tm4525) hypomorphic allele bypasses the requirement of ulp-4 in UPRmt activation.
source: Lastly, expression of ATFS-1 K326R in atfs-1(tm4525) hypomorphic allele bypassed the requirement of ulp-4 in UPRmt activation (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: ATFS-1 is still able to translocate to the nucleus when ULP-4 expression is diminished upon mitochondrial perturbation.
source: Upon mitochondrial perturbation, ATFS-1 was still able to translocate to the nucleus when ULP-4 expression is diminished (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Abolishing SUMOylation site of ATFS-1 (K326R) does not affect subcellular localization of ATFS-1 Δ 1-184.
source: Abolishing SUMOylation site of ATFS-1 (K326R) did not affect subcellular localization of ATFS-1 Δ 1-184 either (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: ulp-4 RNAi greatly reduces the protein level of ATFS-1Δ 1-184.
source: Interestingly, we noticed that ulp-4 RNAi greatly reduced the protein level of ATFS-1Δ 1-184 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that ulp-4 RNAi may affect ATFS-1 expression, or stability.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: After 24 hours, ATFS-1Δ 1-184 level in ulp-4 RNAi treated animals significantly decreases.
source: However, after 24 hours, ATFS-1Δ 1-184 level in ulp-4 RNAi treated animals significantly decreased (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Treating worms with proteasome inhibitor MG132 partially rescues the reduction of ATFS-1 Δ 1-184 under ulp-4 RNAi.
source: Treating worms with proteasome inhibitor MG132 partially rescued the reduction of ATFS-1 Δ 1-184 under ulp-4 RNAi (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that ulp-4 RNAi affects ATFS-1 protein stability.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: ulp-4 RNAi affects ATFS-1 protein stability.
source: Treating worms with proteasome inhibitor MG132 partially rescued the reduction of ATFS-1 Δ 1-184 under ulp-4 RNAi (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that ulp-4 RNAi affects ATFS-1 protein stability.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that proteasome inhibitor rescues ATFS-1 levels under ulp-4 RNAi.

claim: Full-length ATFS-1 levels are reduced under ulp-4 RNAi when worms are treated with lon-1 RNAi.
source: Treating worms with lon-1 RNAi, we showed that full-length ATFS-1 levels were also reduced under ulp-4 RNAi (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Mutation (K326R) that abolishes ATFS-1 SUMOylation partially restores its protein level under ulp-4 RNAi.
source: Mutation (K326R) that abolished ATFS-1 SUMOylation partially restored its protein level under ulp-4 RNAi (Figure 5D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D-E.

claim: Fusion of SMO-1 to mimic SUMOylated form of ATFS-1 significantly reduces its protein level.
source: In contrary, fusion of SMO-1 to mimic SUMOylated form of ATFS-1 significantly reduced its protein level (Figure 5D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D-E.

claim: SUMOylation reduces the stability of ATFS-1.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that SUMOylation reduces the stability of ATFS-1.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective experimental results showing that SUMOylation affects ATFS-1 protein levels.

claim: Mutation of ATFS-1 SUMOylation site greatly enhances its transcriptional activity.
source: We found that mutation of ATFS-1 SUMOylation site greatly enhanced its transcriptional activity, whereas SUMO-mimetic significantly impaired the activity (Figure 5G).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: SUMO-mimetic ATFS-1 significantly impairs its transcriptional activity.
source: We found that mutation of ATFS-1 SUMOylation site greatly enhanced its transcriptional activity, whereas SUMO-mimetic significantly impaired the activity (Figure 5G).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Transcriptions of gpd-2 and gst-14 are blocked by ulp-4 RNAi.
source: Lastly, transcriptions of genes known to be driven by ATFS-1 (eg. gpd-2 and gst-14) (Nargund et al., 2012; Nargund et al., 2015) were blocked by ulp-4 RNAi, which could be partially rescued with ATFS-1 K326R mutation (Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5H and citations to previous studies.

claim: ATFS-1 K326R mutation partially rescues the blockage of gpd-2 and gst-14 transcription by ulp-4 RNAi.
source: Lastly, transcriptions of genes known to be driven by ATFS-1 (eg. gpd-2 and gst-14) (Nargund et al., 2012; Nargund et al., 2015) were blocked by ulp-4 RNAi, which could be partially rescued with ATFS-1 K326R mutation (Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: SUMOylation impairs the transcriptional activity of ATFS-1.
source: Thus, SUMOylation also impairs the transcriptional activity of ATFS-1.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the luciferase reporter assay and qPCR data showing that SUMOylation affects ATFS-1 transcriptional activity.

claim: Worms treated with cco-1 RNAi have a severe synthetic growth defect on ulp-4 RNAi.
source: Indeed, worms treated with cco-1 RNAi had a severe synthetic growth defect on ulp-4 RNAi (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: ulp-4(tm1597) mutants reveal a more severe developmental delay when grown on spg-7 RNAi.
source: Consistently, ulp-4(tm1597) mutants revealed a more severe developmental delay when grown on spg-7 RNAi (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: Mutation of the SUMOylation sites of ATFS-1 and DVE-1 in C. elegans partially rescues the developmental delay of spg-7 mutants.
source: Mutation of the SUMOylation sites of ATFS-1 and DVE-1 in C. elegans partially rescued the developmental delay of spg-7 mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C-E.

claim: The survival rate of worms exposed to high dosage of antimycin is significantly reduced in ulp-4 RNAi.
source: The survival rate of worms exposed to high dosage of antimycin was also significantly reduced in ulp-4 RNAi (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1F-G.

claim: ulp-4 RNAi impairs UPRmt activation when worms are challenged with a Pseudomonas strain.
source: ulp-4 RNAi also impaired UPRmt activation when we challenged worms with a Pseudomonas strain, a mitochondrial insult isolated from the natural habitat of C. elegans (Liu et al., 2014) (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B and citation to a previous study.

claim: ulp-4 RNAi suppresses the activation of immune response and xenobiotic detoxification response.
source: Moreover, ulp-4 RNAi suppressed the activation of immune response and xenobiotic detoxification response (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Deficiency of ulp-4 greatly suppresses the induction of irg-1.
source: We showed that deficiency of ulp-4 greatly suppressed the induction of irg-1 (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Deficiency of ulp-4 impairs worm development when they are infected with Pseudomonas.
source: Deficiency of ulp-4 also impaired worm development and survival rate when they were infected with Pseudomonas (Figure 6E–F) (Kirienko et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E-F and citation to a previous study.

claim: Deficiency of ulp-4 impairs worm survival rate when they are infected with Pseudomonas.
source: Deficiency of ulp-4 also impaired worm development and survival rate when they were infected with Pseudomonas (Figure 6E–F) (Kirienko et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E-F and citation to a previous study.

claim: The reduced survival rate of ulp-4-deficient worms can be rescued with atfs-1 K326R; dve-1 K327R mutations.
source: The reduced survival rate of ulp-4-deficient worms could be rescued with atfs-1 K326R; dve-1 K327R mutations, further demonstrating that deSUMOylation of ATFS-1 and DVE-1 is the major function of ULP-4 during mitochondrial stress (Figure 6G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: deSUMOylation of ATFS-1 and DVE-1 is the major function of ULP-4 during mitochondrial stress.
source: The reduced survival rate of ulp-4-deficient worms could be rescued with atfs-1 K326R; dve-1 K327R mutations, further demonstrating that deSUMOylation of ATFS-1 and DVE-1 is the major function of ULP-4 during mitochondrial stress (Figure 6G).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that mutations preventing SUMOylation of ATFS-1 and DVE-1 rescue ulp-4 deficiency phenotypes.

claim: Under unstressed condition, ulp-4 RNAi does not affect worm lifespan.
source: Under unstressed condition, ulp-4 RNAi did not affect worm lifespan.
evidence: The claim is supported by lifespan analysis data.

claim: ulp-4 RNAi greatly suppresses the lifespan extension in cco-1 RNAi-treated worms.
source: However, ulp-4 RNAi greatly suppressed the lifespan extension in cco-1 RNAi-treated worms, which could be rescued by mutations of SUMOylation site within ATFS-1 and DVE-1 (Figure 6H).
evidence: The claim is supported by lifespan analysis data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Mutations of SUMOylation site within ATFS-1 and DVE-1 rescue the suppression of lifespan extension by ulp-4 RNAi in cco-1 RNAi-treated worms.
source: However, ulp-4 RNAi greatly suppressed the lifespan extension in cco-1 RNAi-treated worms, which could be rescued by mutations of SUMOylation site within ATFS-1 and DVE-1 (Figure 6H).
evidence: The claim is supported by lifespan analysis data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Overexpression of ulp-4 does not affect the basal level of UPRmt under unstressed condition.
source: Overexpression of ulp-4 neither affects the basal level of UPRmt under unstressed condition (Figure 1G), nor affects worm lifespans with or without mitochondrial stress (Figure 6—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Overexpression of ulp-4 does not affect worm lifespans with or without mitochondrial stress.
source: Overexpression of ulp-4 neither affects the basal level of UPRmt under unstressed condition (Figure 1G), nor affects worm lifespans with or without mitochondrial stress (Figure 6—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by lifespan analysis data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1H.

claim: smo-1 RNAi shortens worm lifespan.
source: In contrary, smo-1 RNAi shortened worm lifespan, but greatly extended the lifespan of spg-7 mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by lifespan analysis data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1I.

claim: smo-1 RNAi greatly extends the lifespan of spg-7 mutants.
source: In contrary, smo-1 RNAi shortened worm lifespan, but greatly extended the lifespan of spg-7 mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by lifespan analysis data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1I.

claim: Mutations of SUMOylation site within ATFS-1 and DVE-1 extend lifespan of spg-7 mutants.
